clue.text: Yob, for example, will approve of non-U language

parts.note: to approve of something is to back it
slang is informal speech, the sort not used by the upper class (non-U)

explanation.surface: A lout is sure to like coarse, common talk.
explanation.walkthrough: YOB is BOY spelt backwards, the classic example of back slang. 'Non-U' means not upper-class, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Back slang is a code where words are said reversed, and the word for a lout is a famous instance of it.

clue.text: Players never asked to take a bow?

definitions.text: Players never asked to take a bow?

parts.words: Players never asked to take a bow?
parts.note: the bow is not the performer's bend at the end but the stick string players draw; brass musicians never use one

explanation.surface: Performers who never get invited to acknowledge applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of trumpet, horn and tuba players: their instruments are blown, so none needs a fiddle-style stick.

clue.text: Heard fire — it drops a man

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: Someone hears gunfire and a soldier falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute, often shortened, is what lowers a jumper from an aircraft.

clue.text: Roman bathhouse had to shut out Veronica

indicators.note: shut out tells us the following short word is excluded from the bathhouse's name

parts.note: a sudatorium was the sweating room of a Roman bath
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient baths had to bar a woman called Veronica.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing TO from SUDATORIUM leaves the cloth. St Veronica's veil, with which she wiped Christ's face, is also called a veronica.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudarium is a sweat-cloth, especially the relic veil of St Veronica, itself called a veronica.

clue.text: An annual payment for this land?

parts.note: annual means a year's, abbreviated YRS
hire is the payment made for the use of something

explanation.surface: A question about what yearly rent this territory would fetch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A YR'S HIRE, a year's rental. AYRSHIRE is a county in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrshire is a former Scottish county, a region on the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: Unclean food to hand

parts.note: grub is informal for food
something to hand is by you, nearby

explanation.surface: Dirty food left within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby means dirty or grimy.

clue.text: Sulks, having disease

definitions.meaning: an old word for a fit of sullen silence
a viral illness that swells the glands in the neck

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a bout of sullen moping and the infectious illness causing swollen cheeks.

clue.text: New way to join the Navy

parts.note: a mode is a manner or way of doing something
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A fresh route for signing up as a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up-to-date or recent.

clue.text: Fat horse, fed with poor grain

indicators.note: fed with tells us the horse has the other letters put into it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: poor tells us the letters of grain are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fat horse fed on low-quality grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like a description of the horse, but it is the definition; 'poor' scrambles the grain and 'fed with' puts the result inside the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a spread, an edible fat made from vegetable oils.

clue.text: Addressed the bar

definitions.meaning: ... to someone, the past tense of speak
a rod of a wheel radiating from the hub

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of speak (talked to) and also a rod joining a wheel's hub to its rim.

clue.text: Separate from Anglo-Saxon subordinate

parts.note: someone under another ranks below them

explanation.surface: Distinguishing an Old English underling.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart, into separate pieces.

clue.text: Urged on to travel for experience

indicators.note: to travel tells us the letters of the two words move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is pressed to go abroad to broaden their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel' rearranges the letters of URGED ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through or suffer it.

clue.text: Start to sell fruit, and some asparagus

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A greengrocer begins selling fruit along with asparagus.
explanation.definitionFit: A single shoot of asparagus is called a spear.

clue.text: Breathe in, out, but don't wake up

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to inhale and exhale while staying asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of BREATHE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernating animals sleep through winter without waking.

clue.text: A local politician has eccentric attire

parts.note: taken as written
CC stands for county councillor
outre means bizarre or eccentric

explanation.surface: A councillor turns up in strange clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric attire' looks like the definition, but 'attire' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to dress or equip someone, as to clothe them.

clue.text: Called for calm

definitions.meaning: fetched, as a parent picks up a child

explanation.definitionFit: Picked up (a child from school) and also composed and cool-headed.

clue.text: Fail to take tin-opener, so eat less

parts.note: to die is to fail or stop working
the opener of the word tin is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: Without a can-opener, one must go hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' joins the pieces; 'tin-opener' looks like a kitchen tool but means the opening letter of 'tin'.
explanation.definitionFit: To diet is to restrict food intake to lose weight.

clue.text: Delay, so movie star eats in

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
movie tells us the letters of star are moved about

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Late, because the film star is dining at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movie' scrambles 'star' (moving the letters), and 'in' places the word for eats inside that result. 'so' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is lateness, the state of being slow or delayed.

clue.text: Risk transportation from court

parts.note: chance is risk
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Gambling on deportation from a court.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery was a division of the English High Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Court of Chancery dealt with equity in England.

clue.text: Consolation over exam that may be over one's head

definitions.text: that may be over one's head

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, tells us the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: balm is something soothing or comforting
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: Comfort after an exam whose content was beyond one.
explanation.walkthrough: A balmoral is a Scottish brimless bonnet, named after the royal castle. 'Over one's head' suggests too difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a flat Scottish cap, worn on top of the skull.

clue.text: Trollope's lily of the valley?

definitions.meaning: Lily ... is a heroine of Anthony Trollope's novels
a valley, especially in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: Surname of Trollope's character Lily, and a word for a vale in hill country.

clue.text: Bird in summer diving in the river

indicators.note: diving in tells us the summer piece plunges into the river

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England
heat is the hot season, summer

explanation.surface: A bird plunging into a river in midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Wear flows through Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird of open country.

clue.text: Protect Shakespeare's Fairy Queen

parts.note: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Defend Titania, Shakespeare's fairy queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy Queen' suggests Titania, but the fairy and the queen are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother is to care for and shield someone.

clue.text: Glass-paper

definitions.meaning: the Daily ... is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A looking-glass, and the name of a British tabloid daily.

clue.text: Chant after Julian

definitions.meaning: the calendar that replaced Julius Caesar's

explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong of the Western Church, and the calendar reform that succeeded the Roman one.

clue.text: Half hearted, unintelligible words from actor

indicators.note: half hearted means one of the two middle letters is lost

parts.note: gabble is rapid, unintelligible talk

explanation.surface: A lukewarm actor mumbling his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: GABBLE has BB at its heart; losing half of it leaves the Hollywood star Clark Gable.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Tribesmen's qualifications excellent

parts.note: MAs are Master of Arts degrees
A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Tribal members with top-class degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Tribesmen's' stands for has, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Black Sea resort, so absurdly pretty? Not half!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not half tells us only the first half of the word for absurdly pretty is kept

parts.note: chichi means showily, affectedly pretty

explanation.surface: A resort so ridiculously pretty? Very much so!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much', but here it trims CHICHI to half its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Sochi is a Russian resort city on the Black Sea coast.

clue.text: Cumberland tradesman

definitions.meaning: the Duke of Cumberland, nicknamed for his brutality at Culloden

explanation.definitionFit: Nickname of the Duke who crushed the Jacobites, and a shopkeeper who sells meat.

clue.text: Some fear a chess problem may give a pain in the head

definitions.text: problem may give a pain in the head

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tough chess puzzle can give a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: An earache is pain in the ear, a trouble felt at the side of the skull.

clue.text: Prior or Presbyter

definitions.meaning: an office-bearer in a Presbyterian church

explanation.definitionFit: Older or senior, and a lay official of a Presbyterian church.

clue.text: Percentage made from connections in high places?

definitions.meaning: payments to authors as a share of sales

explanation.definitionFit: Shares of earnings paid to writers, and humorously links with kings and queens.
